title: Refresh token returned in a response body
description: A refresh token issued inside the response body appears in the response body. A refresh token mints new access tokens without the password or the second factor, so one leaked copy extends an intrusion for as long as the token lives.
remediation: Deliver refresh tokens through a scoped, rotating flow and revoke on any anomaly.
limitation: One response body, first 32,768 bytes. It matches the refresh token field with a long value; it cannot tell whether the value behind the marker is live or whether the page needs authentication.
scopeT: A response body that carries a refresh token issued inside the response body.
fp: An acknowledgement that a token was rotated is not reported.
recordDesc: A refresh token issued inside the response body in a response hands every reader the view the build or admin side kept: A refresh token mints new access tokens without the password or the second factor, so one leaked copy extends an intrusion for as long as the token lives.
applicability: Deployments that render a refresh token issued inside the response body into a customer- or partner-facing response.
risk: A refresh token mints new access tokens without the password or the second factor, so one leaked copy extends an intrusion for as long as the token lives.
why: The marker exists for the build or administrator and answers a question an attacker would otherwise have to guess.
fix: Deliver refresh tokens through a scoped, rotating flow and revoke on any anomaly.
Rotate refresh tokens on use and revoke them on any anomaly.
verifyT: Request the page again and confirm the response no longer carries a refresh token issued inside the response body.

title: Identity token claims disclosed with internal roles
description: A decoded identity token whose claims include internal group or role names appears in the response body. The claims name the identity groups a workforce account belongs to, which is the authorisation map an attacker uses to choose a target account.
remediation: Project only the claims the client needs and keep group membership server-side.
limitation: One response body, first 32,768 bytes. It matches the identity token with a role or group claim; it cannot tell whether the value behind the marker is live or whether the page needs authentication.

fp: A token that carries only a subject and an audience is not reported.

risk: The claims name the identity groups a workforce account belongs to, which is the authorisation map an attacker uses to choose a target account.

Project only the claims the client needs and keep groups server-side.

title: One-time code returned in the response
description: The one-time code that was just issued for the step-up check appears in the response body. The code is the second factor, so returning it in the same response as the request removes the factor entirely and lets anyone holding the session complete the step-up.
remediation: Send the code only to the enrolled channel and return nothing but an acknowledgement.
limitation: One response body, first 32,768 bytes. It matches the one-time code field; it cannot tell whether the value behind the marker is live or whether the page needs authentication.
scopeT: A response body that carries the one-time code that was just issued for the step-up check.
fp: A masked field that says a code was sent is not reported.
recordDesc: The one-time code that was just issued for the step-up check in a response hands every reader the view the build or admin side kept: The code is the second factor, so returning it in the same response as the request removes the factor entirely and lets anyone holding the session complete the step-up.
applicability: Deployments that render the one-time code that was just issued for the step-up check into a customer- or partner-facing response.
risk: The code is the second factor, so returning it in the same response as the request removes the factor entirely and lets anyone holding the session complete the step-up.
why: The marker exists for the build or administrator and answers a question an attacker would otherwise have to guess.
fix: Send the code only to the enrolled channel and return nothing but an acknowledgement.
Send the code to the enrolled channel and return only an acknowledgement.
verifyT: Request the page again and confirm the response no longer carries the one-time code that was just issued for the step-up check.

title: OAuth client secret returned in a response
description: An OAuth client id paired with its client secret appears in the response body. The pair lets anyone mint tokens as the application, which usually carries every scope the integration was granted.
remediation: Keep the secret on the server, rotate it, and use proof-of-possession flows for public clients.
limitation: One response body, first 32,768 bytes. It matches the client secret field with a long value; it cannot tell whether the value behind the marker is live or whether the page needs authentication.
scopeT: A response body that carries an OAuth client id paired with its client secret.
fp: A public client with no secret is not reported.
recordDesc: An OAuth client id paired with its client secret in a response hands every reader the view the build or admin side kept: The pair lets anyone mint tokens as the application, which usually carries every scope the integration was granted.
applicability: Deployments that render an OAuth client id paired with its client secret into a customer- or partner-facing response.

why: The marker exists for the build or administrator and answers a question an attacker would otherwise have to guess.
fix: Keep the secret on the server, rotate it, and use proof-of-possession flows for public clients.
Keep the secret server-side, rotate it and use a public-client flow.
verifyT: Request the page again and confirm the response no longer carries an OAuth client id paired with its client secret.

title: API secret returned in a response
description: An API secret key next to its key id appears in the response body. The secret authenticates every signed call the key makes, so a leak lets an attacker replay the integration's authority until the key is rotated.
remediation: Keep the secret in the server key store and rotate it on exposure.
